name: iRAD / eDAR - Integrated Road Accident Database / e-Detailed Accident Report
publisher: MoRTH; built by NIC/NICSI; designed by RBG Labs, IIT Madras; World Bank funded
taxonomy: custom (MoRTH accident recording format; not IPC/BNS)
caveats: no public dashboard, download or API found; dashboards described as for 'higher authorities of stakeholder departments and MoRTH'
coverage ramp-up uneven: 2021-22 sparse for late-adopting states
GPS may be back-filled at the police station rather than captured at the scene; no published positional accuracy
records are FIR-linked and contain personal data - the legal hook for every refusal
DPDP Act 2023 amended RTI s.8(1)(j) removing the public-interest override for personal information
evidence: Search index returned irad.parivahan.gov.in titled 'eDAR India' and a demo instance at gisnic.tn.nic.in/irad/webapp/ titled 'eDAR India Demo'. Secondary sources confirm: MoRTH + World Bank funding, design by RBG Labs IIT Madras, build by NICSI/NIC, integration of Police/Health/Transport/road-owning agencies, on-the-spot mobile capture, all 36 states/UTs onboarded by Nov 2022. No public data access route found. Session egress proxy blocked direct fetch of this host; URL and page title come from a search-engine result, not a guess.
how_to_obtain: (a) RTI to CPIO, MoRTH Road Safety Cell / IT Cell, Transport Bhawan, 1 Parliament Street, New Delhi 110001, asking for: the iRAD/eDAR data dictionary; the data-sharing policy/SOP/MoU and the officer competent to approve access; record counts by state and year; and a CSV of NON-PERSONAL fields only (pseudonymised accident id, date, time, latitude, longitude, road/NH, chainage, severity, collision type, road-user categories, junction type, weather, lighting), with an explicit disclaimer of any request for names, addresses, vehicle numbers, DL numbers or FIR numbers; plus whether coordinates are GPS-captured at scene. (b) Same request in parallel to 3-4 State Transport Commissioners and DGPs - iRAD is federated and states own their records. (c) Academic/MoU route via RBG Labs, IIT Madras or the World Bank task team.
notes: Highest-value target in the entire Crime-map project: national, point-level, near-real-time. File the RTI in week one; the 30-day + appeal + CIC clock is the long pole.

publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs (operated by States/UTs; technology partner C-DAC)
caveats: no public call data found at national or state level

Secondary sources confirm: state-centric deployment, Public Safety Answering Point per state/UT, ten intake channels (voice, SMS, SOS, email, web request, chatbot, media crawler, IoT signals, WhatsApp, external signals), dedicated Emergency Response Centre per state, published response-time commitments (Haryana 15-20 minutes), C-DAC as technology partner. Session egress proxy blocked direct fetch of this host; URL and page title come from a search-engine result, not a guess.
how_to_obtain: State-by-state RTI to the ERSS Nodal Officer / DGP / State Home Department. Request AGGREGATES ONLY to survive the post-DPDP s.8(1)(j): monthly count of 112 calls by emergency category by police station or ERV response zone, and mean/median dispatch and on-scene arrival time by district, for 36 months. Explicitly disclaim any request for caller identity, number, recording or address. Start with a state that already publishes an ERSS dashboard.
notes: Closest thing India has to a real-time incident feed. Response time by ward is the single feature residents most want and never get.
